questions.question: A metal spoon, a wooden block, and a woollen glove are placed on a table in a sealed room maintained at exactly 20 °C. After 48 hours, a student measures the temperature of each object using a contact thermometer. What will the thermometer readings show?
options: The wooden block and woollen glove will be at 20 °C, but the metal spoon will be at a lower temperature because it is a conductor.
The woollen glove will be slightly warmer than 20 °C because it traps heat, while the spoon and wood are at 20 °C.
All three objects will have a temperature of exactly 20 °C.
The metal spoon will be cooler than 20 °C, the woollen glove warmer than 20 °C, and the wooden block exactly 20 °C.

questions.question: When a brass rod is heated from room temperature to 80 °C, its length increases slightly. Which statement correctly explains what happens to the brass particles during this thermal expansion?
options: The particles themselves expand and grow larger, which pushes them further apart.
The average separation between the particles increases because they vibrate more.
New particles are generated within the gaps as energy is absorbed.
The attractive forces between the particles become stronger, pulling them into a larger structure.

questions.question: A cup of hot coffee is left on a desk. As it cools down, energy is transferred from the coffee to the surrounding air. What is happening to the particles in the coffee during this process?
options: Their average speed decreases because they are transferring energy to the air particles.
They slow down because they are losing mass to the air through evaporation.
They maintain the same speed but clump together at the bottom of the cup.
They transfer all their energy to the cup itself, causing the liquid particles to stop moving entirely.

questions.question: A student has two identical mugs containing the same volume of hot water. Mug A is at 90 °C and Mug B is at 50 °C. Both are placed in a room at 20 °C. During the first two minutes, how will the rates of cooling compare?
options: Mug B will cool down faster because its temperature is closer to room temperature.
Mug A will cool down faster because there is a larger temperature difference between it and the air.
Both mugs will cool down at the exact same rate because they have the same volume of water.
Mug B will cool down faster because hot liquids tend to hold their thermal energy longer than warm liquids.

questions.question: Why do different substances, like iron and water, require different amounts of energy to raise the temperature of equal masses by 1 °C?
options: Because the particles in all substances are of equal mass but have different volumes.
Because the mass of the individual particles and the strengths of the attractive forces between them differ.
Because some substances contain particles that do not vibrate when heated.
Because heat energy only affects the surface particles of dense solids like iron.

questions.question: You have two blocks of equal mass: Block X is made of copper and Block Y is made of concrete. Both are heated to exactly 80 °C and then placed into identical containers holding equal amounts of water at 20 °C. Why does the concrete block raise the water's temperature more than the copper block?
options: Concrete is a thermal insulator, so it traps the heat inside the water container.
The same mass of different materials at the same temperature can hold and transfer different amounts of thermal energy.
Copper block particles move much faster than concrete block particles at 80 °C.
Concrete has a lower density, which allows its heat to escape into the water much quicker.

questions.question: Substance A has a specific heat capacity of 4200 J/kg°C, and Substance B has a specific heat capacity of 900 J/kg°C. If you have 1 kg of each substance at exactly 60 °C, which statement about their thermal energy stores is correct?
options: Substance B has more energy in its thermal store because it heats up and cools down much faster.
Substance A has more energy in its thermal store because a higher specific heat capacity means it stores more energy per degree Celsius.
Both substances contain the exact same amount of thermal energy because they are at the same temperature.
Substance A has less energy in its thermal store because its heavier particles require more space to move.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the directions of motion of the particles in a block of ice, a cup of water, and water vapour?
options: The particles in the ice and water move in fixed, predictable paths, while only gas particles move in random directions.
The particles in all three states of matter move or vibrate in random directions.
Only the liquid and gas particles move in random directions; solid particles vibrate in a single, synchronized direction.
The movement is random in gases, circular in liquids, and non-existent in solids.

questions.question: How does the movement of particles in a sample of liquid water change as its temperature rises from 10 °C to 70 °C?
options: The particles begin to move past each other more quickly.
The particles stop moving past each other and begin to vibrate in fixed positions.
The particles expand, causing them to move more slowly due to increased friction.
The particles move in a single, aligned direction rather than randomly.

questions.question: You have two identical steel bolts, Bolt P and Bolt Q. Bolt P is at a temperature of 150 °C, and Bolt Q is at 50 °C. Which bolt has more energy in its thermal store, and why?
options: Bolt P, because for identical objects, the one at the higher temperature contains more thermal energy.
Bolt Q, because lower temperatures mean the particles are more closely packed, storing potential energy.
Both have the same energy because they are identical in material and mass.
Bolt P, because its particles have completely stopped moving, concentrating the heat energy.

questions.question: A small cup of tea and a large teapot of tea are both at exactly 85 °C. How do their thermal energy stores compare?
options: They have the same thermal energy because they are at the same temperature.
The cup of tea has more thermal energy because its particles are concentrated in a smaller volume.
The teapot of tea has more thermal energy because it contains more particles of the substance at that temperature.
The teapot of tea has less thermal energy because the larger volume allows the heat to escape faster.

questions.question: A student wants to measure the temperature of a water bath using a traditional glass thermometer. Which technique is essential to prevent parallax errors when reading the scale?
options: Read the scale from slightly above to ensure you see the meniscus curve.
Hold the thermometer at an angle of 45 degrees to the light source.
Ensure your eye is positioned exactly level with the top of the coloured liquid column.
Remove the thermometer from the water and hold it up to a white background at chest level.

questions.question: If you mix 100 mL of boiling water (100 °C) with 100 mL of ice-cold water (0 °C) in an insulated beaker, which of the following is the most likely final temperature of the mixture?
options: Exactly 100 °C, because hot water is more dominant in thermal transfer.
Exactly 0 °C, because ice-cold water absorbs all available heat instantly.
Around 50 °C, which is cooler than the hot water but warmer than the cold water.
It will fluctuate continuously between 0 °C and 100 °C without settling.

questions.question: A student mixes 400 mL of cold water at 10 °C with 100 mL of hot water at 90 °C. Without doing precise calculations, what can we predict about the final temperature of the mixture?
options: It will be closer to 90 °C than to 10 °C because hot water has more active particles.
It will be exactly 50 °C because mixing always averages the temperatures equally.
It will be closer to 10 °C than to 90 °C because there was a much larger volume of cold water.
It will be lower than 10 °C because the cold water particles slow down the hot ones completely.

questions.question: A cold copper coin at 5 °C is dropped into a mug of hot water at 80 °C. What happens to the speed of the particles in both the coin and the water?
options: The water particles begin to move more slowly, while the coin particles begin to vibrate more quickly.
The water particles begin to move more quickly, while the coin particles begin to vibrate more slowly.
Both the water particles and the coin particles begin to move more slowly as they reach equilibrium.
The water particles maintain their speed, while only the coin particles speed up.

questions.question: One end of a copper rod (a good thermal conductor) is placed in a hot Bunsen burner flame. What do we observe about the temperature along the rest of the rod?
options: The temperature along the rod remains low except at the very tip in the flame.
The temperature along the rod increases quickly as thermal energy is transferred through it.
The temperature along the rod decreases to below room temperature due to conduction currents.
The temperature increases very slowly, taking several hours to change even a few centimeters away.

questions.question: On a microscopic level, how is thermal energy transferred so efficiently through a solid metal conductor?
options: The heated particles physically travel from the hot end of the conductor to the cold end.
Vibrating particles quickly collide with and transfer energy to the particles next to them, causing them to vibrate as well.
The particles in a conductor are fixed and do not vibrate, allowing heat waves to pass through unobstructed.
Hot particles expand and force cold particles out of the conductor into the air.

questions.question: Why does a plastic handle on a hot metal pan remain relatively cool to touch even when the pan is very hot?
options: In plastic, which is an insulator, it is difficult for vibrating particles to cause neighboring particles to vibrate.
Plastic particles do not have any thermal energy stores and cannot vibrate at all.
The plastic handle absorbs heat and instantly converts it into sound energy.
The particles in the plastic handle move away from the heat source to the outer edges.

questions.question: Double-glazed windows feature a thin layer of air trapped between two panes of glass. Why does this design reduce heat loss from a house so effectively?
options: The trapped air absorbs all the heat and reflects it back into the room as light.
Gases like air are very poor thermal conductors, and trapping the air prevents it from transferring heat by moving.
Trapped air particles are packed so tightly together that vibrations cannot pass through them.
The air layer creates a vacuum where particles can no longer vibrate.

questions.question: A student wraps a hot baked potato in a thick layer of bubble wrap, and also wraps a cold can of soda in an identical layer of bubble wrap. What will be the effect of the bubble wrap on each item?
options: It will keep the potato warm by stopping heat loss, and keep the soda cold by stopping heat from entering.
It will warm up both the potato and the soda because bubble wrap generates its own thermal energy.
It will cool down both the potato and the soda by trapping cold air around them.
It will keep the potato warm but will cause the cold soda to warm up much faster than normal.

questions.question: A wooden desk, a metal chair, and a plastic cup have been sitting in a draught-free, sealed classroom at 20 °C for over 24 hours. Which statement correctly compares their temperatures?
options: The metal chair is the coldest, the plastic cup is the warmest, and the wooden desk is in between.
All three objects have exactly the same temperature of 20 °C.
The wooden desk and plastic cup are at 20 °C, but the metal chair is slightly colder because metal is a conductor.
Their temperatures cannot be determined without knowing their starting temperatures before they were put in the room.

questions.question: When a solid copper block is heated from 20 °C to 80 °C, what happens to the individual copper particles and the spacing between them?
options: The individual particles expand in size, while the spacing between them remains completely constant.
The individual particles do not change size, but the average separation between them increases.
The individual particles shrink, allowing more particles to crowd together and increase the density.
The individual particles stop vibrating, which allows them to drift further apart.

questions.question: A tight brass ring is stuck on a steel rod. To remove the brass ring, an engineer decides to heat the brass ring quickly. Why does this method work?
options: Heating the brass ring causes its particles to vibrate more, making the ring expand and loosen from the rod.
Heating causes the brass particles to pack more tightly together, making the ring larger in thickness but wider in diameter.
Heating causes the brass particles to lose mass, allowing the ring to slide off easily.
Heating causes the steel rod to shrink while the brass ring remains at a constant volume.

questions.question: A hot mug of cocoa is left on a table. As it cools down, energy is transferred from the cocoa to the surrounding air. What happens to the speed of the particles in the cocoa and the air during this process?
options: The cocoa particles begin to move less quickly, while the air particles move more quickly.
The cocoa particles begin to move more quickly, while the air particles move less quickly.
Both the cocoa particles and the air particles begin to move less quickly.
The speed of the cocoa particles remains constant, while the air particles slow down.

questions.question: Two identical mugs contain the same volume of coffee. Mug A is at 90 °C in a room at 20 °C, while Mug B is at 40 °C in the same room. Which mug will experience the faster rate of temperature drop in the first minute, and why?
options: Mug B, because it is closer to the room temperature and requires less energy loss to cool down.
Mug A, because the greater temperature difference between the coffee and the air causes a faster rate of cooling.
Both mugs will cool down at the same rate because they have the same volume of coffee.
Mug A, because hot particles are heavier than cooler particles and fall out of the liquid faster.

questions.question: Why do equal masses of iron and water behave differently when heated with the same amount of energy?
options: Iron particles have the same mass as water particles, but iron particles do not experience attractive forces.
Water and iron have different particle masses and different attractive forces between their particles.
The particles in water are completely stationary, whereas the particles in solid iron move freely.
Iron particles expand when heated, whereas water particles shrink when heated.

questions.question: A chef wants to heat 1 kg of vegetable oil and 1 kg of water from 20 °C to 80 °C. What must the chef do to achieve this, given that oil and water are different substances?
options: Apply the exact same amount of heating to both, as they have the same mass and starting temperature.
Provide different amounts of heating because different substances require different amounts of energy to reach the same temperature.
Heat the water less than the oil, because water particles are inherently hotter than oil particles.
Heat only the oil, because oil is a thermal insulator and will automatically heat the water through contact.

questions.question: You have two blocks of the same mass and temperature: Block X is made of copper, and Block Y is made of wood. If both are placed into separate identical beakers of cold water, they cause different amounts of temperature rise in the water. Why does this happen?
options: Copper and wood have different temperatures, even though they are measured at the same value.
The same amount of different materials at the same temperature can store and transfer different amounts of energy.
The wood block dissolves in the water, which prevents any energy from transferring.
Copper particles destroy energy as they cool, whereas wood particles create energy.

questions.question: Substance A has a specific heat capacity of 4200 J/kg°C, and Substance B has a specific heat capacity of 900 J/kg°C. If you have 1 kg of each substance at 50 °C, which one has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Substance B, because its lower specific heat capacity allows its particles to move much faster.
Substance A, because a higher specific heat capacity means 1 kg of the substance stores more energy at a given temperature.
Both have the same energy because they are at the exact same temperature and have the same mass.
Neither substance has any thermal energy because they are both below 100 °C.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the movement of particles in solids, liquids, and gases?
options: Particles in gases move randomly, but particles in liquids and solids move in highly organised, predictable patterns.
The directions in which particles move or vibrate are random in solids, liquids, and gases alike.
Only liquid particles move randomly; solid particles do not move at all, and gas particles move only upwards.
Particles in solids vibrate randomly, but liquid and gas particles only move in straight lines parallel to gravity.

questions.question: If the temperature of a substance is steadily increased, what happens to the motion of its particles?
options: The particles vibrate faster in a solid, or move past each other faster in a liquid or gas.
The particles begin to move in fixed circular paths rather than random directions.
The particles slow down in order to absorb and store the extra heat energy.
The particles in a solid start to spin, while those in a gas completely stop moving.

questions.question: Two identical iron frying pans are on a stove. Pan A is at 180 °C, and Pan B is at 80 °C. Which frying pan has more energy in its thermal store, and why?
options: Pan B, because lower temperatures mean the particles are more closely packed and can store more energy.
Pan A, because for two identical objects, the one at a higher temperature has more energy.
They have the same thermal energy because they are identical in mass and material.
Pan A, because the particles have grown larger in size, which increases their total mass.

questions.question: Two copper blocks, Block P and Block Q, are both at a temperature of 60 °C. Block P has a mass of 2 kg, while Block Q has a mass of 0.5 kg. Which block contains more thermal energy?
options: Block P, because it has more particles of the same substance at the same temperature, so it has more energy.
Block Q, because the smaller mass allows the particles to pack together more tightly and vibrate faster.
Both blocks contain the same amount of thermal energy because their temperatures are identical.
Block Q, because less energy is wasted keeping a large mass warm.

questions.question: When measuring the temperature of a liquid with a glass laboratory thermometer, how should you position your eyes to get an accurate reading?
options: Look down at the thermometer from slightly above to see the shape of the liquid surface clearly.
Your eye must be level with the top of the coloured liquid column to avoid parallax errors.
Look up at the thermometer from below to make sure you can see the scale markings clearly.
It does not matter where your eye is positioned as long as the thermometer is held completely still.

questions.question: If you mix 400 ml of hot water at 80 °C with 100 ml of cold water at 20 °C in an insulated jug, what can you predict about the final temperature of the mixture?
options: The final temperature will be exactly 50 °C, which is the perfect average of the two temperatures.
The final temperature will be closer to 80 °C than to 20 °C, because there was more of the hot water.
The final temperature will be closer to 20 °C, because cold water has a stronger cooling effect than hot water.
The final temperature will rise above 80 °C due to the friction of mixing.

questions.question: A cold metal spoon at 5 °C is placed into a bowl of hot soup at 70 °C. What happens to the speed of the particles in the soup and the spoon?
options: The particles in the soup move more slowly, while the particles in the spoon move more quickly.
The particles in both the soup and the spoon move more quickly.
The particles in the soup move more quickly, while the particles in the spoon move more slowly.
The particles in the spoon stop moving completely, transferring all their energy to the soup particles.

questions.question: You heat one end of a long rod made of a thermal conductor. What do you observe happening to the temperature along the rod?
options: The temperature along the conductor increases quickly as energy is rapidly transferred along it.
The temperature at the heated end rises, but the rest of the rod remains cold forever.
The temperature increases very slowly, taking hours for any change to reach the other end.
The temperature along the rod decreases because conductors convert heat into light.

questions.question: At a microscopic level, how does a thermal conductor transfer energy along its length so quickly when heated?
options: Vibrating particles quickly cause the particles near to them to vibrate as well.
The particles at the hot end travel physically from one end of the conductor to the other.
The particles in a conductor shrink, allowing empty space to carry heat radiation.
The particles stop vibrating entirely, allowing heat waves to pass through unimpeded.

questions.question: Double-glazed windows and fiberglass loft rolls both contain trapped air. Why does trapped air make them highly effective insulators?
options: Air is a solid that blocks any movement of heat particles through physical barriers.
Gases are very poor thermal conductors, so trapping air prevents effective energy transfer.
Trapped air particles move much faster than free air particles, which destroys cold energy.
Trapped air causes the surrounding materials to contract and become denser, blocking heat.

questions.question: A camper wraps a hot bottle of soup in a thick woolen blanket. Later, they use the same clean blanket to wrap a cold bottle of ice water. What effect does the blanket have in both cases?
options: It heats up the hot soup and warms up the ice water.
It cools down the hot soup and keeps the ice water cold.
It keeps the hot soup warm and keeps the cold ice water cool by reducing energy transfer.
It has no effect on either bottle because wool only works on living organisms.

questions.question: A metal spoon, a wooden table, and a plastic cup have been sitting in a room at 20 °C for 24 hours. Which statement correctly describes their temperatures?
options: The metal spoon is colder than 20 °C, the wooden table is at 20 °C, and the plastic cup is warmer.
All three objects have reached exactly the same temperature of 20 °C.
The wooden table and plastic cup are at 20 °C, but the metal spoon is slightly colder because metal is a conductor.
The objects will never reach the exact same temperature unless they are in direct contact with each other.

questions.question: When a block of copper is heated from 20 °C to 80 °C, what happens to its particles?
options: The individual copper particles grow larger in size, taking up more space.
The spacing between the copper particles increases, while the size of the particles themselves remains constant.
The particles move closer together because the bonds between them strengthen.
The particles vibrate so much that they slide past each other, but their average separation remains unchanged.

questions.question: An engineer designs a concrete bridge with small gaps between the concrete slabs. Why is this design necessary when considering temperature changes?
options: To allow the slabs to contract without cracking during hot summer days.
To prevent the slabs from pushing against each other and warping when they expand during hot weather.
To make sure water drains easily so that the concrete particles can absorb moisture and shrink.
To allow the air between the slabs to heat up and increase the overall mass of the bridge.

questions.question: A hot mug of tea is placed on a table in a cool room. Over time, the tea cools down. What is happening at the particle level during this process?
options: The tea particles transfer energy to the surrounding air particles, causing the tea particles to slow down and the air particles to speed up.
Cold particles from the air enter the mug and slow down the rapid movement of the tea particles.
The tea particles lose mass as they cool, which reduces their overall speed of movement.
The air particles transfer their cold energy to the tea particles, which causes the tea particles to stop vibrating.

questions.question: Two identical cups containing different amounts of hot coffee are placed in the same room at 20 °C. Cup A starts at 90 °C and Cup B starts at 50 °C. Which cup cools down faster initially, and why?
options: Cup B cools faster because it is closer to the room temperature, requiring less energy transfer to reach equilibrium.
Cup A cools faster because the greater temperature difference between it and the room results in a more rapid rate of energy transfer.
Both cups cool at the exact same rate because they are in the same room and contain the same liquid.
Cup B cools faster because smaller temperature differences allow particles to transfer energy more efficiently.

questions.question: If you supply the exact same amount of thermal energy to 1 kg of water and 1 kg of copper, the copper will undergo a much larger temperature increase than the water. What does this demonstrate?
options: Water has a lower capacity to store thermal energy than copper.
It is easier to increase the temperature of copper than it is to increase the temperature of water.
Copper particles are much lighter and therefore need less energy to move at all.
Thermal energy always increases the temperature of solids more than liquids.

questions.question: Why do different substances, such as iron and water, require different amounts of heating to raise their temperatures by the same amount?
options: Because the mass of their individual particles and the strengths of the attractive forces between them are different.
Because solids have no spaces between their particles, whereas liquids have large empty gaps.
Because some substances contain particles that can be easily destroyed by heating.
Because the temperature of water is naturally fixed, whereas metals can have any temperature.

questions.question: You have two insulated containers: one has 1 kg of water at 80 °C, and the other has 1 kg of iron at 80 °C. If each is used to heat up a separate, identical block of ice, why does the water melt significantly more ice than the iron does?
options: Water is a liquid and can flow around the ice to transfer heat, whereas the solid iron cannot.
The same mass of water and iron at the same temperature can cause different amounts of heating.
Iron particles have a higher starting speed than water particles at the same temperature.
Water contains more mass than iron when they are at the same temperature.

questions.question: Substance X has a specific heat capacity of 4,200 J/kg°C, and Substance Y has a specific heat capacity of 800 J/kg°C. If you have 1 kg of each substance at 50 °C, which statement is true?
options: Substance Y contains more energy in its thermal store because its particles are more tightly bound.
Substance X contains more energy in its thermal store than Substance Y at this temperature.
Both substances contain the exact same amount of thermal energy because they are at the same temperature.
Substance Y will take longer to cool down to room temperature than Substance X.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the direction of movement of particles in different states of matter?
options: Particles in solids move randomly, but particles in liquids and gases follow predictable, structured paths.
Particles in gases move randomly, but particles in solids and liquids do not move in random directions.
The directions in which particles move or vibrate are random in solids, liquids, and gases.
Particles only move randomly when a substance is heated above its boiling point.

questions.question: As the temperature of a substance increases, what change occurs to the movement of its particles?
options: The particles in a solid vibrate faster, while particles in a liquid or gas move past each other more quickly.
The particles in a solid stop vibrating, while particles in a liquid begin to move in straight, fixed lines.
The particles in a liquid slow down to prevent the substance from expanding too quickly.
Only gas particles speed up; solid and liquid particles maintain a constant speed but change their direction.

questions.question: You have two identical copper blocks, Block A and Block B, with the same mass. Block A is at 90 °C, and Block B is at 30 °C. How do their energy stores compare?
options: Block B has more energy in its thermal store because cooler particles can pack more tightly together.
Both blocks contain the exact same amount of energy because they are made of the exact same material and have the same mass.
Block A has more energy because, for two identical objects, the one at a higher temperature has more energy.
Block A has less energy because heating a substance causes its particles to escape, reducing its stored energy.

questions.question: Container A contains 100 ml of water at 60 °C, and Container B contains 500 ml of water at 60 °C. Which container's water has more energy in its thermal store, and why?
options: Container A, because the thermal energy is more concentrated in a smaller volume of water.
Container B, because it has more particles of the same substance at the exact same temperature.
Both have the same thermal energy because their temperatures are identical.
Container B, because the water particles in larger volumes move much faster than in smaller volumes.

questions.question: To obtain an accurate temperature reading using a traditional liquid-in-glass thermometer, how should a student position themselves?
options: Look down at the thermometer from a high angle to see the curved surface of the liquid clearly.
Look up from below the thermometer scale to ensure the lowest numbers are visible.
Ensure their eye is perfectly level with the top of the coloured liquid column.
Hold the thermometer at arm's length and tilt it slightly to catch the light.

questions.question: A student mixes 100 ml of water at 80 °C with 100 ml of water at 20 °C. What can be predicted about the final temperature of the mixture?
options: The final temperature will be exactly 100 °C as the temperatures of the two liquids add together.
The final temperature will be cooler than 20 °C because mixing disrupts the kinetic energy of the particles.
The final temperature will be cooler than 80 °C but warmer than 20 °C.
The final temperature will remain at 80 °C because the hot water particles dominate the mixture.

questions.question: If you mix 500 ml of water at 90 °C with 100 ml of water at 20 °C, what will be true about the final temperature of the mixture?
options: The final temperature will be exactly halfway between 90 °C and 20 °C.
The final temperature will be closer to 90 °C because there was more of the hot water.
The final temperature will be closer to 20 °C because cold water is denser and absorbs heat faster.
The final temperature will exceed 90 °C because of the rapid collision of particles during mixing.

questions.question: A cold metal spoon at 5 °C is placed into a bowl of hot soup at 75 °C. What happens to the movement of the particles in both substances?
options: The soup particles speed up, and the spoon particles slow down.
The soup particles slow down, and the spoon particles speed up.
The particles in both the soup and the spoon speed up as they collide.
The particles in both the soup and the spoon slow down to reach equilibrium.

questions.question: Why does the temperature along a metal rod increase so quickly when one end of it is held in a flame?
options: The heat melts the metal particles, allowing them to flow rapidly to the cold end.
The hot air from the flame travels through hollow channels inside the metal rod.
The vibrating particles at the hot end quickly cause the particles near to them to vibrate as well.
The metal particles at the hot end swap places with the cold particles at the other end.

questions.question: Double-glazed windows consist of two panes of glass separated by a layer of trapped air. Why does this design make the window a good thermal insulator?
options: Gases are very poor thermal conductors, and trapping the air prevents it from transferring heat easily.
The trapped air layer absorbs all the cold particles before they can reach the inner pane.
Glass is a highly effective thermal conductor, so the air is only there to keep the glass panes stable.
The air layer allows thermal energy to radiate back outside at a much faster rate.

questions.question: Why is a thick thermal sleeve useful both for keeping a hot coffee mug warm and for keeping a cold can of soda cold?
options: The sleeve generates its own heat for the coffee and absorbs coldness from the soda can.
The sleeve acts as an insulator, slowing down the transfer of thermal energy both into the cold soda and out of the hot coffee.
The sleeve increases the surface area, which allows the ambient room temperature to stabilize the drinks.
The sleeve prevents particles from evaporating from the surface of both containers.

questions.question: A metal spoon, a wooden block, and a plastic cup are left on a table in a room kept at 20 ºC for 24 hours. If we measure their temperatures, what will we find?
options: The metal spoon will be the coldest because metals naturally feel colder than wood and plastic.
The metal spoon, wooden block, and plastic cup will all have a temperature of exactly 20 ºC.
The plastic cup will have the highest temperature because plastic is a good thermal insulator.
The temperatures will still depend on the material, with the wooden block having the intermediate temperature.

questions.question: A copper rod is heated at one end. Which of the following best describes what happens to the particles at the heated end of this solid?
options: The particles start moving freely from one end of the copper rod to the other.
The particles stop moving entirely as they absorb the thermal energy.
The particles begin to vibrate more quickly in their fixed positions.
The particles expand in size, causing them to squeeze closer together.

questions.question: A beaker of water is heated on a Bunsen burner. What happens to the water particles as the temperature of the liquid increases?
options: They begin to vibrate in fixed positions and can no longer slide past each other.
They move around more quickly, increasing their average speed.
They break down into hydrogen and oxygen gas particles instantly.
They stay at the same speed but get much heavier.

questions.question: When a solid brass ball is heated, it can no longer pass through a metal ring that it easily slid through when cold. Why does the separation of the particles change to cause this?
options: The particles themselves expand and grow larger, reducing the gaps between them.
The particles vibrate more vigorously, causing their average separation to increase.
The particles lose energy, which makes them repel each other and pack tighter.
The particles escape the solid and form a gas layer around the ball, increasing its volume.

questions.question: An engineer leaves small gaps between rails on a railway track. Which physical phenomenon of solids is this design intended to safely accommodate during hot summer days?
options: The contraction of the rails when they absorb thermal energy.
The expansion of the rails as heating causes them to take up more space.
The melting of the rails into a liquid state due to solar radiation.
The sudden increase in the mass of the rails as they get hotter.

questions.question: A hot cup of tea is left on a desk. As it cools down, energy is transferred from the tea to the surrounding air. What happens to the movement of the particles in the tea during this process?
options: They begin to move less quickly as they transfer energy to the air particles.
They stop moving entirely once the tea's temperature falls below 50 ºC.
They begin to move more quickly because they are losing mass.
They maintain the exact same speed, but the air particles slow down.

questions.question: Two identical cups of coffee are made. Cup A is at 90 ºC, and Cup B is at 50 ºC. Both are placed in a room where the air temperature is 20 ºC. Which cup will experience the fastest initial rate of cooling?
options: Cup B, because it is closer to room temperature and needs less energy to cool down.
Cup A, because the greater temperature difference between it and the air causes it to cool down faster.
Both will cool down at the exact same rate because they contain the same volume of liquid.
Cup A, because hot liquids have a lower density which speeds up conduction.

questions.question: You have 1 kg of water and 1 kg of copper. You want to raise the temperature of both by 10 ºC. Why does the copper reach this temperature much faster when heated with the same source?
options: Because all substances require the exact same amount of energy, but copper conducts it faster.
Because it is easier to increase the temperature of some materials, like copper, than others, like water.
Because copper particles are much lighter and therefore cannot absorb energy.
Because water is an insulator and cannot change its temperature at all.

questions.question: Why do different substances have different thermal behaviors, such as requiring different amounts of energy to raise their temperature?
options: Because some substances do not contain particles and are completely continuous.
Because the mass of particles and the attractive forces between particles are different in different substances.
Because some substances have particles that are completely stationary even at high temperatures.
Because the particles in metals are always twice as large as the particles in non-metals.

questions.question: Two different blocks, one made of iron and one made of aluminium, have the same mass. To raise both blocks from 20 ºC to 50 ºC, what is true about the heating required?
options: They need the exact same amount of heating because they have the same mass and starting temperature.
Different substances need different amounts of heating to reach the same temperature.
The aluminium block will not require any heating because it is a lightweight metal.
Only the iron block will require heating because metals with higher density heat up automatically.

questions.question: Two identical insulated containers hold equal masses of different liquids at 80 ºC: Container X has water and Container Y has oil. If you use each to heat up identical cold metal blocks, the block placed in Container X reaches a higher temperature. Why?
options: Because the same amount of different materials at the same temperature can cause different amounts of heating.
Because water particles are larger than oil particles and physically push heat into the block.
Because oil is a thermal conductor and retains all its heat, preventing transfer.
Because water always cools down faster than oil regardless of the temperature difference.

questions.question: Substance A has a higher specific heat capacity than Substance B. If you have 1 kg of each substance at the same temperature, what does this tell you about their thermal stores?
options: Substance B has more energy in its thermal store because its particles are heavier.
Substance A has more energy in its thermal store because a higher specific heat capacity means 1 kg of a substance has more energy at a given temperature.
Both substances have the exact same amount of energy in their thermal stores because their temperatures and masses are equal.
Neither substance has any energy in its thermal store because they are below boiling point.

questions.question: Compare a solid iron block at 100 ºC and an identical solid iron block at 20 ºC. How does the behavior of the particles in the hotter block compare to the colder one?
options: The particles in the 100 ºC block vibrate faster than the particles in the 20 ºC block.
The particles in the 100 ºC block move freely around the block, whereas in the 20 ºC block they are fixed.
The particles in the 100 ºC block are larger and heavier than those in the 20 ºC block.
The particles in both blocks vibrate at the exact same speed, but the hotter block has more particles.

questions.question: You have two identical copper spheres. Sphere A is at a temperature of 80 ºC, and Sphere B is at a temperature of 30 ºC. Which sphere has more energy in its thermal store, and why?
options: Sphere B, because cooler objects store energy more efficiently.
Sphere A, because for two identical objects, the one at a higher temperature has more energy.
They have the same amount of energy because they are made of the same substance and have the same mass.
Neither sphere has any energy because they are both solids.

questions.question: Two blocks of copper are both at a temperature of 25 ºC. Block X has a mass of 2 kg, while Block Y has a mass of 0.5 kg. Which block has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Block Y, because its smaller mass allows the particles to vibrate with less resistance.
Block X, because for two objects made of the same substance at the same temperature, the one with more particles has more energy.
Both blocks have the same energy because their temperatures are identical.
Neither block has any thermal energy because 25 ºC is close to room temperature.

questions.question: When measuring the temperature of a liquid using a glass thermometer, how must you position yourself to get an accurate reading?
options: You must look down at the thermometer from above to see the depth of the liquid.
Your eye needs to be level with the top of the coloured liquid in the glass tube.
You must hold the thermometer at arm's length and tilt it at a 45-degree angle.
You must read the scale from below the level of the liquid to account for reflection.

questions.question: A student mixes 400 ml of hot water at 80 ºC with 100 ml of cold water at 20 ºC. What can be predicted about the final temperature of the mixture?
options: The final temperature will be exactly 50 ºC, because it is the halfway point.
The final temperature will be closer to 80 ºC because there was more of the hot water.
The final temperature will be closer to 20 ºC because cold water is more dense and dominates the mixture.
The final temperature will be above 80 ºC due to the friction of mixing.

questions.question: A cold metal spoon is placed into a hot bowl of soup. What happens to the particles of the soup and the spoon?
options: The soup particles begin to move more slowly, and the spoon particles begin to vibrate more quickly.
The soup particles begin to move more quickly, and the spoon particles begin to vibrate more slowly.
Both the soup and spoon particles speed up as they gain energy from the surroundings.
The soup particles stop moving entirely, while the spoon particles melt.

questions.question: Why does a metal rod conduct heat much faster than a wooden rod when one end is placed in a flame?
options: In the metal conductor, vibrating particles quickly cause the particles near to them to vibrate as well.
Metal contains hollow channels that allow hot air to flow quickly to the other end.
The wood particles are so tightly packed that they cannot vibrate at all.
Metal particles are magnetic and attract heat energy from the air.

questions.question: Why are double-glazed windows, which contain a layer of air trapped between two panes of glass, highly effective at reducing heat loss from a house?
options: Because air is a solid that blocks all forms of particle movement.
Because materials that contain trapped air provide good insulation, as gases are very poor thermal conductors.
Because the trapped air speeds up the convection currents to push heat back inside.
Because glass and air combine to form a vacuum which destroys thermal energy.
